newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end up on U.S. trends, banks jump.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end up on U.S. trends, banks jump.

text.p: Swedish shares rose on Friday, supported by favourable U.S. trends.
The general index rose 1.37 percent to 2,377.24 in relatively low turnover of 3.24 billion crowns.
Dealers described trading as calm as many players had taken the day off ahead of the three-day weekend holiday.

Banking groups S-E-Banken and Nordbanken were in focus after a Friday newspaper article said Investor, the Wallenberg family's investment arm, could buy 20-25 percent of the state's stake in Nordbanken, paving the way for a merger of the banks.
Nordbanken jumped 5.5 crowns to 221, while S-E-Banken rose 2.5 to 70.5 crowns and Investor rose 4.5 to 299.5.
"It is hard to see any large deals when all just is rumours," said on trader. "The market is soon saturated with rumours about banking mergers." But several analysts believe in a merger.
Other banks also rose, Swedbank ending at 118.5 crowns, up five, and Foreningsbanken rose 0.90 crown to 35.6, while Handelsbanken rose two to 196.
The bank sector was the clear winner, up 2.25 percent.
